result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md in full (independently, not from CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary). Checks performed: (1) Zero implementation code -- exhaustively scanned every fenced code block (lines 153,161,182,195,216,231,239,249,267,275,295,308,317,328,349,357,372,376,450,454,485,521). Every block contains only interfaces, type aliases, and bare function signatures ending in ';' or handler stubs with a literal '{ ... }' body placeholder -- no real if/return/comparison/arithmetic statement appears inside any code block. All behavior (parseStaffCommandArgs's token rule, checkEventStaffAuthorization's 4-step predicate, the handler sequences in 4.1-4.3) is stated as prose numbered steps or markdown tables outside the code fences, matching the accepted REQ-016/017 pattern -- this defect class (the one that FAILed REQ-016 and REQ-017 previously) is not present here. (2) Schema/precedent claims verified against the actual repo, not trusted: apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts:289-308 confirms event_staff has exactly id/event_id/user_id/created_at/updated_at plus uq_event_staff_event_user(event_id,user_id) and no revoked_at/removed_at column, matching the design's claim. apps/bot/src/domain/venue.ts:418-441 deleteVenue confirmed byte-for-byte as the cited precedent (one DELETE + one writeAuditLog in one db.transaction) that section 1's hard-delete reasoning and section 2.4's removeEventStaff design mirror. apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts confirmed to already export requireOrganizerForChapter/checkOrganizerForChapter/resolveActingUser exactly as the design describes reusing unchanged. apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts:729 confirms isFinished(endsAt, evaluationTime) exists and is reused, not reimplemented. apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts's exports (resolveOrCreateUser, getFlowUserByTgId, getUserWithChapterByTgId) confirm getUserByTgUsername is genuinely new, and schema.ts's index list confirms users.tg_username has no unique index -- both matching the design's own claims (section 2.2, open question 3). git grep -n "speaker" apps/bot/src returned no matches and git grep -n "registration.*list|listRegistrations" apps/bot/src returned no handler match -- both confirm the design's own stated grep results (section 0.5, section 6 item 5) rather than trusting them asserted. (3) All 6 ACs verified against section 7's map: AC1 (cross-event refusal) -> checkEventStaffAuthorization step 2, staffRow existence keyed on the exact (event_id,user_id) pair. AC3 (post-ends_at refusal) -> step 3, reusing isFinished unchanged -- verified reused, not reimplemented. AC4 (bilingual notification on assign and remove) -> 4.1 step 10 / 4.2 step 9, resolveLangForTg on the TARGET's own tgId, sent via ctx.api.sendMessage. AC5 (exactly one audit_log row per assign/remove) -> 2.4's addEventStaff/removeEventStaff, each one db.transaction containing exactly one writeAuditLog call alongside exactly one row mutation -- matches the deleteVenue-verified precedent shape, so this is buildable as stated, not aspirational. AC6 (no speaker read) -> section 0.5, and independently confirmed via the git grep above -- nothing in the four new/touched files has any reason to reference speaker/Talk data. (4) Security invariants: checkEventStaffAuthorization's predicate (section 3.2) never inspects user.role at any of its 4 steps -- traced this myself against the printed rule table, confirming the 'no role short-circuit' claim is real, not asserted: an owner/organizer with no event_staff row for the exact event is refused at step 2 identically to a member. This genuinely closes S2's negative case (EventStaff for event 1 reaching event 2) via AC1, and section 0.4's claim that assignment never writes users.role is correct by inspection of addEventStaff's stated behavior (INSERT into event_staff only) -- so the three organizer-only handlers' existing checkOrganizerForChapter gate is untouched and still excludes an EventStaff-only user, which is what AC2 needs. No new design-system token/class is referenced anywhere (section 8) -- correctly N/A, consistent with REQ-016/017's own precedent that the bot surface has no visual component; nothing to validate against tokens.css for this requirement. (5) AC2 'registration list' gap -- resolved as (b), acceptable scope note, not a MAJOR blocking issue. Reasoning: AC2 names three organizer-only surfaces; two (venue create /venue_new, event publish /event_publish) exist today and this design correctly demonstrates, by inspection of the actual authorization code path (section 0.4, verified against eventAuthorization.ts), that an EventStaff-only user is refused on both with zero code change needed. The third (registration list) does not exist anywhere in this codebase -- confirmed independently via git grep above, not merely CODE-DESIGNER's assertion. This is a completeness gap in the requirement text's own testability (AC2 names a surface that has not been built by any prior requirement), not a design defect: CODE-DESIGNER correctly named it as an open question (section 6 item 5) rather than silently omitting it or inventing a stub handler out of scope. The authorization principle AC2 is actually testing -- that EventStaff status confers no role-derived permission -- is structurally guaranteed by the design's own convention (decisions/0004's 'no domain logic in handler bodies' plus the established pattern of every organizer-only handler calling requireOrganizerForChapter as its first check, per section 0.1's reasoning and eventAuthorization.ts's real code): any future organizer-only handler, registration-list included, would have to deliberately deviate from this codebase's only established authorization pattern to grant EventStaff-only access, which is a much higher bar than 'forgetting a check.' Verifying the principle against the two handlers that exist is therefore a legitimate (if partial) test of the same mechanism, not a different mechanism. This does not, however, make AC2 as literally worded fully testable today -- flagging as a MINOR issue for the record: REQ-ANALYST should be asked to either amend REQ-018's AC2 wording to name only the two currently-existing surfaces, or explicitly annotate the third as deferred-until-built, so TEST-DESIGNER at Step 3 does not have to independently rediscover this same gap.

issues.description: REQ-018's AC2 names three organizer-only surfaces (venue create, event publish, registration list) but 'registration list' has no handler anywhere in this codebase yet (confirmed via git grep). The design correctly documents this and argues the underlying authorization principle still holds by construction, but AC2 as literally worded cannot be fully exercised until a future requirement builds that handler. Recommend REQ-ANALYST amend REQ-018's AC2 text to name only the two currently-buildable surfaces, or explicitly scope the third as verified structurally rather than by direct test, so TEST-DESIGNER does not have to rediscover this gap at Step 3.
